title: An Update on the Health Effects of Tomato Lycopene - PMC
abstract: A phase II clinical trial was performed in men (n = 71) diagnosed with prostate cancer investigating the effects on PSA levels of a tomato extract capsule (Lyc-o-Mato®, 15mg/day lycopene) consumed twice daily for up to 6 months with or without soy isoflavones (Vaishampayan et al. Epidemiological studies suggest that higher intake of lycopene is associated with either a reduced risk of lung cancer (Yuan et al. In a prospective cohort study of 3182 free-living subjects in rural Japan, higher serum levels of lycopene were significantly associated with a reduced risk of colorectal cancer mortality (Ito et al. In contrast, a number of observational studies from the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, and Japan found no association between lycopene intake or plasma lycopene levels and gastric cancer risk (Botterweck et al. In a more recent study, 18 healthy men and women consumed a soy-tomato beverage daily (21 mg lycopene/day) for eight weeks (Bohn et al.
